stage1.impression: A night view through a dark steel-framed window into a deep timber-and-concrete bar, with records at left, a counter, and a pair of small pale boxes on the far wall. Warm and moody, but it reads as CG: the floor is a smeared, mottled denoiser reflection, the steel mullions carry a blotchy game-texture patina, and the speakers that should be the hero are tiny, flat, cream-white rectangles with no acrylic or tint. A magazine would not run it as a specific place; it reads as a generic dark bar, because the shopfront's own signatures (the etched name, the dancing-woman lightbox, the Dome pendants, the altar) are not legible.

blocking_9: The altar pair reads at a glance as smoked cast acrylic with a resin horn and glow through the cabinet, not as flat cream boxes (speaker faces lum_p95 below 140 with visible internal gradient).
The shopfront itself is the subject: the etched name on the glass and the frosted dancer lightbox are both visible and legible in frame.
The floor reads as polished concrete with aggregate and a clean, soft reflection, with no mottled denoiser smear.
The blackened steel reads as steel at 1:1: near-black, a soft uneven sheen, crisp edges, and patina at real scale rather than large blotches.
The Dome pendants read as lamps over the counter, with pools on the zinc, and no bare clipped disc.
The light is the room's own: no street wash brightening the floor toward the camera.
Some sign of life is readable from the kerb (a glass, a coat, a figure at the counter).

defects.what: The altar speakers read as pale cream rectangles with a white disc. They are overlit by the 1200 W spots, with no smoked tint, no acrylic depth and no horn shape; they read as PA monitors, not the hero.
The floor reflection is mottled and smeared like denoiser blotches. It is the brightest large area (median 58) and brightens toward the window (falloff bins 48 to 73), so it is lit from the street.
The steel mullion has a blotchy, large-scale patina texture with white flecks and soft edges. It reads as a game texture.
The thin steel mullion has the same blotchy texture and is slightly soft.
A bare, hot circular disc with 27.8% of its pixels clipped. It reads as a stray bulb or a CG light, not a Dome pendant; no Dome pendants are legible over the counter.
No etched name is visible on the glass (emission 0.0, and no raking light catches it). The shopfront's main identifier is missing.
The frosted dancer lightbox is not identifiable. The right bay shows a pale panel and a timber-looking pillar with a smeared vertical gradient; the silhouette does not read.
A bright warm sill or kerb strip (median 146) at the bottom edge pulls the eye out of frame.
Identical stools repeated with no sign of use. The room reads empty, like a showroom.
A crushed corner (crush 42.7%) with a soft, ghostly downlight cone on the wall above the right bay.

out_of_scope.request: Give the altar pair a saturated tint so the frame has its one colour.
out_of_scope.why: The Smoke configuration is fixed as the house tint; under Smoke the frame will stay near-monochrome and the speaker must win on light and form, not colour.

out_of_scope.request: Make the dancer lightbox larger or move it so it reads from the kerb.
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront's design is fixed; only the camera (c4) and its brightness may change.
